result.narrative:
Shrivana Textile Mills is showing broadening payment stress rather than an isolated dispute. There are three open overdue notifications across two TCI policies: two items totalling INR 42.0M under the whole-turnover policy TCI-WT-2026-0001, with the oldest at 50 days past due, and one item of INR 9.5M at 34 days past due under the supply-chain-finance policy TCI-SCF-2026-0001. The payment review records days-late on resolved invoices worsening across three cycles (10 to 14 to 22 days) and notification volume doubling in the last six months (4 versus 2), now spanning both policies at once. A single article dated 2026-10-24 reports that two banks are reviewing exposure after the company sought longer credit on working-capital lines, with export orders from two European retailers cut this quarter.

The score is 71.9, in the High Risk band, from 0.65 x 70.0 (payment, 50 DPD) + 0.35 x 75.6 (news) — 45.5 weighted payment plus 26.4 weighted news, implying a PD of 0.7212. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and the underwriter should read them before acting. The band is load-bearing on one leg: payment evidence alone at 45.5 would sit in Watch, and the news leg does not hold the band on its own, yet that 26.4 rests on a single anonymously sourced report in publication "Illustrative" with no named lender and no corroboration. The adjudicator also found the payment review does not reconcile — it states INR 21.0M open against notifications recording INR 42.0M and INR 9.5M, its INR 11.0M oldest invoice cannot be traced, and its "newly overdue 31-60 day tranche (4.0M)" is unsourced. Those errors run toward more exposure, not less, so the "remains within the aggregate 100.0M credit limits" reassurance should not be relied on. The article carries age_days 30 while the latest payment notification is dated 2026-10-20, so actual DPD may be higher than the 50 days scored.

The recommendation on both lines is REDUCE to the amount currently owed, cutting each to the limit where expected loss meets the 25% appetite against a PD of 0.7212. On TCI-WT-2026-0001 (insured Velaris Polymers), the limit goes from INR 80,000,000 to INR 42,000,000, taking expected loss from 41,541,120 to 21,809,088. On TCI-SCF-2026-0001 (insured Meridia Bank), the limit goes from INR 20,000,000 to INR 9,500,000, taking expected loss from 10,385,280 to 4,933,008. Maximum liability does not bind on either line. Given the reconciliation gap, confirm the true open balance against the aggregate INR 100.0M limit and re-run the score on current payment data before the action goes out.

Moving to Watch requires the score to fall 21.9 points, below 50.0. The clearest route is cure of the overdue items — settlement of the INR 42.0M at 50 DPD and the INR 9.5M at 34 DPD, with days-late reversing the 10-14-22 trend. On the news side, the lender-exposure report either being disproven, or the company confirming renewed working-capital lines and restored export orders, would remove a leg the band currently depends on; left alone it decays only slowly, on a 365-day half-life.
